title: Orchestrator Active Session
description: The shape of registry/active-session.json — the checked-in seed of a session's mutable state. The seed is committed with every value null or empty on purpose: a session file carrying one developer's active repo is a session file that quietly redirects the next person's commands. The live values are written under ~/.orchestrator/state/, outside every repository, so a terminal, a CI job, and the view plane read the same bytes.

$schema.description: Relative path to this schema. Present so an editor can validate the file as it is typed.

sessionVersion.description: Semantic version of this session shape. Required, because a reader that cannot tell an old session file from a new one will happily interpret a missing field as a false value rather than as 'written before this field existed'.

lastUpdated.description: ISO-8601 UTC timestamp of the last write, or null in the committed seed. Null means 'never written', which is different from 'written and empty'.

activeRepo.description: Name of the repo in focus, matching a name in registry/connected-repos.yml. Null means no repo has been selected, in which case the tooling falls back to the workspace folder name and says so — an inferred repo that announces itself is recoverable, a silent one is not.

activeGroup.description: Name of the group in focus, matching a group in registry/connected-repos.yml. Null when work is single-repo.

activeMode.description: Which context profile loads at session start. The three values match CONTEXTS in scripts/_lib.py and the files under contexts/; adding a fourth here without adding the context file produces a mode that loads nothing and reports no error.

lastCommand.description: The most recent orchestrator command, for resuming after a compaction or a crash.

lastQuery.description: The most recent user query, retained for the same reason. Treat it as untrusted text on read: it is user input that has been round-tripped through a file, and re-injecting it into a prompt is exactly the delayed-injection surface the memory write guard exists to close.

history.description: Recent session events, newest last. Bounded by the writer, not by this schema — an unbounded history is a file that grows until the session-start read stops fitting in the budget.

pinnedRepos.description: Repos the user has pinned; these stay near the top of any picker regardless of recency.

recentRepos.description: Most-recently-active repos, newest first. Separate from pinnedRepos because recency decays and a pin does not.

loadedMemory.description: What memory the current session has already pulled in. Tracked so a refresh is a decision rather than a reflex — re-reading shared memory on every turn is a straightforward way to spend the eager-context budget on text that has not changed.

globalMemoryLoaded.description: Whether memory/shared/ has been loaded this session.

repoMemoryLoaded.description: Repo names whose memory/repos/<name>/ content has been loaded this session.

lastMemoryRefresh.description: ISO-8601 UTC timestamp of the last refresh, or null if memory has not been loaded.

qualityGates.description: The quality floor for this session and the outcome of the last gate. Required at the top level so a session file can never be silently gate-less.

minScore.description: The passing score a review or test phase must reach, on the 0-100 scale the reviewer and QA agents produce. Defaults to 80, matching the `gate` values in config/pipeline-graph.json. Setting it to 0 disables the gate for the session; that is a legitimate move during setup work and a visible one, which is the point of storing it here rather than in an environment variable nobody reads back.

lastScore.description: The score the most recent gate produced, or null if no gate has run.

lastGateResult.description: Outcome of the most recent gate. `escalated` is distinct from `fail`: it means the failure count reached maxGateFailuresBeforeEscalation and the decision moved to a human, so a retry loop must not treat it as another ordinary failure and try again.

budget.description: The last context-budget measurement. Every figure here is an ESTIMATE derived by dividing characters by charsPerTokenEstimate in config/token-budgets.json — it is not a tokenizer count, and anything reporting these numbers should say so. This system deleted a fabricated token-savings percentage from its source material and does not intend to grow another one.

lastEagerChars.description: Characters of always-on and eager context measured at the last budget run, or null if none has run.

lastEstimatedTokens.description: lastEagerChars converted at the configured chars-per-token estimate. An estimate of an estimate; useful for spotting a jump, not for billing.

lastOverBudget.description: Whether the last measurement exceeded the configured eager budget. False when no measurement has run, which is indistinguishable from 'measured and fine' — check lastEagerChars for null before reading anything into it.
